The Hebbian principle, also known as Hebb's rule, states that "neurons that fire together, wire together" (Hebb, 1949). This concept was first introduced by Canadian psychologist Donald Hebb, who proposed that the strength of a neural connection between two neurons is increased when they are activated simultaneously. In other words, the more two neurons are co-activated, the stronger their connection becomes.
